name: H2 Database
tagline: Fast pure-Java SQL engine for embedded, in-memory and test databases, with compatibility modes.
description: H2 is a compact relational database written in Java that runs embedded in the JVM, in pure in-memory mode, or as a TCP/PG server. It is the default test database for Spring Boot and many Java frameworks because it starts in milliseconds and offers compatibility modes that imitate PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, SQL Server and others closely enough for most ORM-level tests. The MVStore engine gives MVCC transactions and file persistence, and the 2.x line has steadily improved SQL standard coverage. It remains actively maintained with regular releases, but it is not a production server for high concurrency or large data.
developer: H2 Group (Thomas Mueller, Evgenij Ryazanov and contributors)

scale.notes: Designed for a single JVM; databases of a few GB are comfortable.

strengths: Starts in milliseconds; ideal for unit and integration tests
Compatibility modes for PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, SQL Server, DB2 dialects
Single small JAR with built-in web console
In-memory and file-backed modes share the same SQL
Java functions and triggers run in-process
weaknesses: Compatibility modes are approximations; tests can pass on H2 and fail on the real database
Major versions change the file format, requiring export/import
Not designed for concurrent multi-user production workloads
useCases: Embedded storage in Java desktop tools
Prototyping before choosing a production database
In-memory scratch databases in batch jobs
